Repo: c:\Users\Micro\3D Objects\DEV\deliveryhub_white_label (frontend React/Vite) + git submodule server_delivery (NestJS backend). Supabase Postgres.

I'm planning a big new "módulo RESTAURANTE" feature (dine-in: mesas/comandas/garçons/impressoras por setor/KDS telas cozinha+bar/PDV caixa). Need to understand the EXISTING kitchen display screen ("tela da cozinha") and order/product data model before designing new per-item routing to printers/sectors.

Please read and report on:
1. Find the existing kitchen/KDS screen — likely under `src/pages/restaurante-dashboard/` or similar (search for "cozinha", "preparo", "kitchen", status like "preparing"/"em preparo"). Report the file path(s), what statuses an order/item goes through, and how the frontend polls/subscribes for updates (websocket? polling interval? Supabase realtime?).
2. The `orders` table schema and any `order_items`/`order_products` table — find the migration file(s) that define them. Report all columns, especially any status field, and whether status is tracked per-order only or per-item.
3. `products` table schema (migration file) — all columns, e.g. name, price, category, image, and whether there's already anything like a "printer"/"station"/"setor" field.
4. Any existing printing utility beyond `src/utils/printComanda.js` (already partially read — it has `printFichaMotoboy` and a generic `printIframe` helper). Check the rest of that file (lines 40-154) and search for other usages of `printIframe` or window.print in the frontend, to see if there's a pattern for printing a kitchen ticket already.
5. Search for how orders reach the kitchen screen today — is there a customer-tracking page (QR/link) that shows live order status? Look for `src/pages/order-tracking` or similar, and report its data source/polling pattern, since a new dine-in QR tracking page (per Ideia 13) would likely mirror it.

Report file paths, table schemas (columns/types), and the polling/realtime pattern used for live status updates. Cite file:line for key facts. Under 600 words.

content.text:
I have enough to write the report.

## Report

**1. Kitchen (KDS) screen** — `src/pages/restaurante-cozinha/index.jsx` (529 lines), backed by `src/services/cozinhaPortalService.js` (token-based portal API) and `src/services/restauranteService.js` (owner-session API).

- Statuses shown: only `confirmed` ("Aguardando Preparo" → next: `preparing`) and `preparing` ("Em Preparo" → next: `ready`) — `STATUS_INFO` object, index.jsx:16-19. Advancing calls `atualizarStatusPedido`/`atualizarStatusCozinhaPortal` (PATCH `/api/cozinha-portal/pedidos/:id/status`, cozinhaPortalService.js:36-40).
- Status is **per-order only** (`pedido.status`), not per-item — items (`pedido.itens`) just render name/qty (index.jsx:70-77), no per-item status.
- Update pattern: **polling every 30s** (`setInterval(() => carregar(...), 30000)`, index.jsx:259/272) **plus Supabase Realtime** subscription on `postgres_changes` for table `orders` filtered by `restaurant_id` (index.jsx:279-289), which triggers a full reload rather than pushing item-level deltas.
- Also has barcode/scan-to-find (`buscarPorId`), and auto-print of new orders (footer text index.jsx:524), printer name stored in `localStorage` via `printComanda.js`.

**2. `orders`/`order_items` schema** — defined in `supabase/migrations/20250825103853_setup_rls_policies.sql:68-88`, evolved by later migrations.

`orders`: `id BIGSERIAL`, `customer_id`, `restaurant_id`, `total NUMERIC(10,2)`, `status TEXT` (CHECK, per-order only), `payment_method`, `user_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. Status enum was extended over time: base `('pending','confirmed','ready','out_for_delivery','delivered','canceled')` → `preparing` added in `20260607000006_add_preparing_status.sql`; `motoboy_collecting` added in `20260609000001_motoboy_collecting_realtime.sql`. Other order-level columns added later: `troco_para`, `entrega`/`pagamento` fields, `cancel_reason`, `comprovante_pix`, `frete_cobrado`, motoboy geo fields (`motoboy_lat`, `motoboy_lng`, `motoboy_location_at`) referenced in order-tracking-status/index.jsx:184-192.

`order_items` (line 80-88): `id`, `order_id` (FK orders, CASCADE), `product_id` (FK products, RESTRICT), `quantity INTEGER`, `unit_price NUMERIC(10,2)`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. **No status column at all** — no per-item tracking exists today. This is the key gap: a KDS with per-item routing to printers/sectors will need a new status (and sector/station) column on `order_items`.

**3. `products` schema** — base at lines 44-54 of same migration: `id`, `name`, `description`, `price NUMERIC(10,2)`, `image_url`, `is_active BOOLEAN`, `category_id` (FK categories). Extended: `tipo` ('normal'/'promo'/'combo'), `preco_promo`, `destaque` (`20260606000002_add_aparencia_e_produto_tipo.sql`); `restaurant_id` direct FK (`20260610000005_products_restaurant_id.sql`); tags/combos (`20260610000002/3/4`). **No printer/station/setor field exists anywhere** — grep across `supabase/migrations` for printer|station|setor|kds found nothing. This confirms it needs to be added new (e.g., a `setor`/`station_id` column on `products` or a join table for multi-printer routing).

**4. Printing utilities** — `src/utils/printComanda.js` full file (154 lines): shared `printIframe`-style pattern is actually duplicated inline (not exported) — `printFichaMotoboy` (lines 11-58) and `printComanda` (lines 80-154) each build hidden `<iframe>`, write ticket HTML+CSS (thermal-printer style, JsBarcode CDN for barcode, QR via api.qrserver.com), then `window.print()` inside the iframe and auto-remove it. Also exports `barcodeValue`, `getPrinterName`/`setPrinterName` (localStorage `kitchen_printer_name`). Only 6 files use these prints: `restaurante-financeiro`, `restaurante-dashboard/index.jsx`, `restaurante-dashboard/PedidoDetalhe.jsx`, `restaurante-dashboard/RelatorioPanel.jsx`, `restaurante-cozinha/index.jsx`, and printComanda.js itself. There's no separate printer-routing/multi-station logic — one ticket per whole order, single printer (name stored globally, not per-sector).

**5. Customer order-tracking page** — `src/pages/order-tracking-status/index.jsx` (295 lines). Data source: fetches `GET /api/pedidos/:id` (Nest backend) with Supabase auth bearer token (lines 42-49), receiving `{ pedido, itens, cliente, empresa, pagamento_pago }`. Live updates: Supabase Realtime `postgres_changes` UPDATE on `orders` filtered by `id=eq.${orderId}` (lines 65-75), **plus 30s fallback polling** guarded to stop once status is `delivered`/`canceled` (lines 77-87). This realtime+30s-polling-fallback pattern is the one a new dine-in QR tracking page should mirror; note it's currently gated behind Supabase auth session (line 38-40), so a public/anonymous QR page for dine-in customers would need a token-based variant like the `cozinha_token` portal pattern instead.
